text:
sara: quick heads-up — during the spike this morning we saw a lot of requests fall back to the tiny-quant model even though the route should have matched the tenant-specific model. looks like header normalization is stripping `x-tenant-priority` before route match. anyone seen this pattern before? :thinking:

james: ugh. i remember a similar one — our gateway normalizes headers (lowercase + strip duplicates) in the auth middleware which runs before route-matching. if the route match relies on exact-case or presence of that header it can lose it.

maria: can we whitelist a small set of headers to preserve raw value until route matching completes? `x-tenant-priority` and `x-routing-hint` maybe. less risk than moving matching later.

kevin: whitelist SGTM. also we should safeguard with an explicit fallback ranking so even if headers get lost we prefer the larger model rather than tiny-quant. current fallback list is [tiny-quant, small-quant, default] which explains the behavior. change to [small-quant, tiny-quant, default] for now.

sara: good call. two parallel asks: (1) whitelist headers pre-route-match, (2) flip fallback preference for capacity-pressure paths. can someone propose the minimal config diff?

james: here's a minimal gateway snippet — land this patch in gateway-config:```yaml
route_matchers:
  - name: tenant-priority-header
    type: header
    header: x-tenant-priority
    preserve_raw: true
    regex: '^(high|med|low)$'
  - name: path-prefix
    type: prefix
    prefix: /v1/tenant
fallback_policy:
  capacity_paths:
    - id: prefer_small_then_tiny
      order: [small-quant, tiny-quant, default]
```

maria: add telemetry too: emit metric `fallback_choice{tenant,route}` and a `header_preserved` boolean so we can track how often the whitelist actually helped. that's necessary before we roll this to prod.

kevin: +1. and add a circuit-breaker rule: if fallback_rate for a tenant > 5% for 5m, temporarily pin that tenant to dedicated pool or block tiny-quant fallback to avoid quality cliffs. we'll need a console alert rule for that.

sara: routing/console UX note — in the rollout UI can we surface a simulated request runner that shows which matcher fired and what fallback chain would be chosen? makes testing config changes safer. pinging @deploy-bot to run a canary once config is ready.

deploy-bot: deploy request received. starting canary for gateway-config patch `whitelist-header-preserve-216543` to shard-a. will report summary to this thread when done. :robot_face:

james: i'll open a PR with the snippet + unit tests for header preservation and fallback ordering. will include a small integration test that hits the canary endpoint with variants of the header.

maria: i'll add the fallback_choice metric and a dashboard tile (percent fallback by tenant, top 10 tenants) — also an alert for >5% for 5m as kevin suggested.

kevin: if the canary looks good let's ship tonight but leave TTL=1h for the whitelist change so we can revert quickly if something weird happens.

sara: thanks team. assign owners: james -> gateway PR, maria -> metrics + dashboard, kevin -> circuit-breaker rule + alert, me -> rollout + canary coord. we'll reconvene after deploy-bot posts canary results. :thumbsup:
